title: Alleluia, Hymn of Sweetness
description: Alleluia, Hymn of Sweetness in Tonic Solfa to MANNHEIM, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Latin hymns of the early Church for Hymns of the Early Church (London, 1896), headed “Alleluia, Dulce Carmen”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Eights and Sevens, six lines (8.7.8.7.8.7), and this page sets them to MANNHEIM; any other Eights and Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Al-le-lu-ia, hymn of sweet-ness, Joy-ful voice of cease-less praise; Al-le-lu-ia, plea-sant an-them, Choirs ce-les-tial sweet-ly raise: This the song of those a-bid-ing In the house of God al-ways.

lines: Alleluia, hymn of sweetness,
Joyful voice of ceaseless praise;
Alleluia, pleasant anthem,
Choirs celestial sweetly raise:
This the song of those abiding
In the house of God always.
Alleluia, Mother Salem,
All Thy people joy in song;
Alleluia, walls and bulwarks
Evermore the notes prolong:
Ah! beside the streams of Babel,
Exiled, weep we o’er our wrong.
Alleluia, ’tis befitting
That our song should falter here;
Alleluia, can we sing it
When the clouds of wrath appear?
To bemoan our sin with weeping,
Now the time is drawing near.
Trinity, for ever blessed!
May we sing the gladsome lay,
When from sin our souls are severed,
And the clouds have passed away,
And we share the Easter glory,
In the realms of endless day?

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Early Church (1896)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Latin, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Early Church; set to MANNHEIM by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
